habitat: Pairs in coastal bush, riverine forest, forest fringes and broad-leaved woodland. It perches in the middle layer and often returns to the same perch.
summary: A fairly common resident. Blue-grey, and told from Grey Tit-Flycatcher by its behaviour and the lack of white in the tail. The immature has spotted upperparts and mottled underparts. The call is a short descending phrase, and it is mostly silent. The Kemp name Bluegrey Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Grey Tit-Flycatcher has white outer tail feathers and fans its tail.

upperparts.pattern: Blue-grey, with no white in the tail.

viewNotes.note: Blue-grey, with no white in the tail.

calls.description: A short descending 'tsip-tsip-tsip-tsip-tse-tslipip', but mostly silent. The grade A call is from Kruger near Skukuza. The filename does not name the species.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Blue-grey is not a single colour name. The grade A call is from Kruger and the filename does not name the species. The Kemp name Bluegrey Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.
